segments.narration: Divers found the crew still seated at their stations. Eight men. Inside a Confederate submarine that had been missing on the seabed since 1864.
February 1864, off Charleston. The Hunley drove a spar torpedo into the USS Housatonic, sinking it in three minutes. History's first submarine kill.
Then it never came home. Twenty-one men died inside this boat across three separate sinkings. So what killed the final eight?
Located in 1995, raised in 2000. No skeleton showed injury. The pump was never set to clear water. Nobody had released the escape weights.
In 2017 Duke researchers named the likely killer: their own torpedo. A hundred and thirty-five pounds of powder, sixteen feet away. The blast wave went through the hull, and through them.

verdicts.claim: When the H. L. Hunley was recovered, the remains of its eight crewmen were found seated at their stations, the submarine having been lost since 1864.

verdicts.claim: On 17 February 1864 the Hunley drove a spar torpedo into the USS Housatonic off Charleston, sinking it in about three minutes — the first warship sunk by a submarine.
verdicts.note: 89% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 2 number(s)

verdicts.claim: The Hunley sank three times and 21 men died aboard it in total, eight of them in the third and final loss.
verdicts.note: 77% of the claim's wording appears in the reference article, including 1 number(s)

verdicts.claim: The wreck was located in 1995 and raised on 8 August 2000; the skeletons showed no trauma, the bilge pump was not set to clear water, and the keel release weights had never been released.
verdicts.note: Located April 1995 by Ralph Wilbanks (NUMA), raised 8 August 2000; 2008 finding on the unset pump and 2018 finding on the unreleased keel blocks both reported.

verdicts.claim: A 2017 Duke University study in PLOS ONE concluded the crew were most likely killed by the blast of their own 135-pound torpedo, detonated less than 16 feet from the bow.
verdicts.note: Lance et al., PLOS ONE, August 2017: 135-lb black powder charge less than 16 ft from the bow, blast wave transmitted through the hull, immediate fatal lung trauma most likely. Narration says 'likely killer' because NHHC archaeologists dispute the conclusion.
